verses.zh: 非利士人将他们的军旅聚到亚弗；以色列人在耶斯列的泉旁安营。
verses.en: The Philistines assembled all their troops[NOTE:1] at Aphek, while Israel camped at the spring that is in Jezreel.
verses.commentary:
29:1 "to Aphek" This word (BDB 67) has an uncertain etymology, possibly

- "river bed," KB 80

- "stronghold," KB 80, BDB 67

- "enclosure" (from VERBAL root), BDB 67

There are several places/cities by this designation

- on the coast near Joppa

- on the coast near Acco

- east of the Sea of Galilee

- on the eastern Philistine border south of Timnah

- Aphekah, southwest of Hebron

- Aphekah, east of Byblos

A good atlas picture is in The MacMillan Bible Atlas, p. 74, map #95. BDB says it is the same city
as mentioned in Josh. 12:18 (cf. 1 Kgs. 20:26,30; 2 Kgs. 13:17).

verses.zh: 非利士人的首领各率军队，或百或千，挨次前进；大卫和跟随他的人同着亚吉跟在后边。
verses.en: When the leaders of the Philistines were passing in review at the head of their units of hundreds and thousands,[NOTE:1] David and his men were passing in review in the rear with Achish.
notes: Heb “passing by with respect to hundreds and thousands.” This apparently describes a mustering of troops for the purpose of inspection and readiness.
verses.commentary:
29:2 "the lords" This is a Philistine loan word (BDB 710). It refers to the "kings" of the five city-states of the
Philistine area (cf. v. 7; 1 Sam. 5:8).

▣ "by hundreds and by thousands" These are not numbers only but military groupings.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

verses.zh: 非利士人的首领说：「这些希伯来人在这里做甚么呢？」亚吉对他们说：「这不是以色列王扫罗的臣子大卫吗？他在我这里有些年日了。自从他投降我直到今日，我未曾见他有过错。」
verses.en: The leaders of the Philistines asked, “What about these Hebrews?” Achish said to the leaders of the Philistines, “Isn’t this David, the servant of King Saul of Israel, who has been with me for quite some time?[NOTE:1] I have found no fault with him from the day of his defection until the present time!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “from the day of his falling [away] until this day.”
verses.commentary:
29:3 "the commanders" This is a generic term (BDB 978) for "chieftain," "ruler," "official," "captain," "prince."
Here, it refers to the Philistine military commanders.

▣ "Hebrews" This (BDB 720, KB 782) term is mostly used by non-Israelite people to designate Israelites.
Its etymology seems to be "one from the other side," possibly referring to "those coming from the eastern side of the
Jordan (i.e., not from Canaan).

- "Eber" of Gen. 10:24-25, a descendant of Shem

- "Habiru," a semi-nomadic Semite population migrating from east to west across the ANE in
the second millennium (see El-Amarna Letters)

▣ "rather these years" The LXX makes this time period specific (i.e.," this is the second year"), possibly
following 1 Sam. 27:7.

▣

NASB NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA
"deserted"

TEV, REB
"came over"

NJB
"gave himself up"

Peshitta
"came"

NET
"defection"

The MT has "fall" (BDB 656, KB 709, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)
used in the metaphorical sense of "falling away from Saul." This VERB is used of desertion
before an enemy in Jer. 37:13; 38:19.

verses.zh: 非利士人的首领向亚吉发怒，对他说：「你要叫这人回你所安置他的地方，不可叫他同我们出战，恐怕他在阵上反为我们的敌人。他用甚么与他主人复和呢？岂不是用我们这些人的首级吗？
verses.en: But the leaders of the Philistines became angry with him and said[NOTE:1] to him, “Send the man back! Let him return to the place that you assigned him! Don’t let him go down with us into the battle, for he might become[NOTE:2] our adversary in the battle. What better way to please his lord than with the heads of these men?[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and the leaders of the Philistines said.”
Heb “so that he might not become.”
Or perhaps, “our men.” On this use of the demonstrative pronoun see Joüon 2:532 §143.e.
verses.commentary:
29:4 "were angry with him" The Philistine military leaders had a negative emotional reaction to David and his men because

- of their relation to Israel (i.e., racial animus)

- of their fear of them helping the Israelite army (i.e., military strategy)

From the text, both seem true.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RACISM

▣ "the man" This is a way of showing disrespect. They will not even mention David's name.

▣

NASB, NRSV, LXX
"Would it not be with the heads of these men?"

NKJV, JPSOA
"if not with the heads of these men?"

TEV
"by the death of our men?"

REV
"than at the price of our lives?"

Peshitta
"except with our heads?"

In this period and in this part of the world, victory was expressed by the cutting off of the
heads of the vanquished foes or enemy.

- Goliath ‒ 1 Sam. 17:46,51

- Saul ‒ 1 Sam. 31:9

- Ish-bosheth ‒ 2 Sam. 4:7

- Sheba ‒ 2 Sam. 20:22

- Elisha, charge of the intent of the king of Israel ‒ 2 Kgs. 6:31-32

verses.zh: 从前以色列的妇女跳舞唱和说：『扫罗杀死千千，大卫杀死万万』，所说的不是这个大卫吗？」
verses.en: Isn’t this David, of whom they sang as they danced,[NOTE:1] “‘Saul has struck down his thousands,but David his tens of thousands’?”
verses.commentary: 29:5 The Philistines knew of David's military prowess.

verses.zh: 亚吉叫大卫来，对他说：「我指着永生的耶和华起誓，你是正直人。你随我在军中出入，我看你甚好。自从你投奔我到如今，我未曾见你有甚么过失；只是众首领不喜悦你。
verses.en: So Achish summoned David and said to him, “As surely as the Lord lives, you are an honest man, and I am glad to have you[NOTE:1] serving[NOTE:2] with me in the army.[NOTE:3] I have found no fault with you from the day that you first came to me until the present time. But in the opinion[NOTE:4] of the leaders, you are not reliable.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “it is good in my eyes.” Cf. v. 7.
Heb “your going forth and your coming in.” The expression is a merism.
verses.commentary:
29:6 "As the Lord lives" This is an oath idiom based on the covenant
name for Israel's Deity (YHWH). It is so surprising that a Philistine king would use this name!

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ Notice how Achish describes David's perceived loyalty.

- you have been upright

- his goings out and comings in have been pleasing to the Philistines (i.e., his supposed raids on southern Judah,
cf. v. 8; 1 Sam. 26:8-11)

- Achish had not found evil in anything David had done for all his time with him

- David is described as "like an angel of God" (v. 9; 2 Sam. 14:17,20; 19:27)

However, also note the two "nevertheless" (vv. 6, 9). Even with all this praise, the Philistine
military leaders will not allow David and his men to join the battle.

verses.zh: 现在你可以平平安安地回去，免得非利士人的首领不欢喜你。」
verses.en: So turn and leave[NOTE:1] in peace. You must not do anything that the leaders of the Philistines consider improper!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and you must not do evil in the eyes of the leaders of the Philistines.”

verses.zh: 大卫对亚吉说：「我做了甚么呢？自从仆人到你面前，直到今日，你查出我有甚么过错，使我不去攻击主―我王的仇敌呢？」
verses.en: But David said to Achish, “What have I done? What have you found in your servant from the day that I first came into your presence until the present time, that I shouldn’t go and fight the enemies of my lord the king?”

verses.zh: 亚吉说：「我知道你在我眼前是好人，如同　神的使者一般；只是非利士人的首领说：『这人不可同我们出战。』
verses.en: Achish replied to David, “I am convinced that you are as reliable[NOTE:1] as the angel of God! However, the leaders of the Philistines have said, ‘He must not go up with us in the battle.’
notes: Heb “I know that you are good in my eyes.”

verses.zh: 故此你和跟随你的人，就是你本主的仆人，要明日早晨起来，等到天亮回去吧！」
verses.en: So get up early in the morning along with the servants of your lord who have come with you.[NOTE:1] When you get up early in the morning, as soon as it is light enough to see, leave.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The LXX and a couple of Old Latin mss include here the following words: “and you shall go to the place that I have appointed you. Don’t place an evil thing in your heart, for you are good before me.”
Heb “when you get up early in the morning and you have light, go.”
verses.commentary:
29:10 These is some confusion in the Hebrew text of this verse (JPSOA footnote). The LXX has an
expanded version.

"And now be early in the morning, you and the servants of your Lord who came with you, and go to the place,
there where I appointed you, and do not place a pestilent thought in your heart, for you are good before me,
and start early on the way, and let there be light upon you, and go."

The UBS Text Project, p. 203, gives the LXX version a "D" rating (highly doubtful), but
they prefer it to the MT.

▣ "of your lord" This must be a reference to King Saul. It was another way of asserting that David
and his men were Hebrews/Israelites.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why are the Philistines and Israelites fighting so far north?

- What is the origin of the designation "Hebrew"?

- Why did the Philistine military generals distrust David?

- Why is David compared to "an angel of God"?

verses.zh: 于是大卫和跟随他的人早晨起来，回往非利士地去。非利士人也上耶斯列去了。
verses.en: So David and his men got up early in the morning to return[NOTE:1] to the land of the Philistines, but the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
notes: Heb “to go in the morning to return.” With the exception of Origen and the Lucianic recension, the Old Greek tradition lacks the phrase “in the morning.” The Syriac Peshitta also omits it.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 29:1-5

1Now the Philistines gathered together all their armies to Aphek, while the Israelites were
camping by the spring which is in Jezreel. 2And the lords of the Philistines were proceeding
on by hundreds and by thousands, and David and his men were proceeding on in the rear with Achish.
3Then the commanders of the Philistines said, "What are these Hebrews doing here?" And
Achish said to the commanders of the Philistines, "Is this not David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel,
who has been with me these days, or rather these years, and I have found no fault in him from the day he
deserted to me to this day?" 4But the commanders of the Philistines were angry with him,
and the commanders of the Philistines said to him, "Make the man go back, that he may return to his place
where you have assigned him, and do not let him go down to battle with us, or in the battle he may become
an adversary to us. For with what could this man make himself acceptable to his lord? Would it not be with
the heads of these men? 5Is this not David, of whom they sing in the dances, saying,

'Saul has slain his thousands,

And David his ten thousands'?"
